newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil states turn to Congress on debt woes - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil states turn to Congress on debt woes - paper.

text.p: The governors of 19 Brazilian states have decided to abandon talks with the Finance Ministry on renegotiating their debts, opting instead to turn proposals into bills to put before Congress, a local newspaper said.

Folha de S. Paulo said the governors, who met Monday in Sao Paulo, feel talks with ministry officials about how to reduce their debts, which total some 100 billion reais ($98 billion), have been fruitless.
"We no longer want to talk to ministerial offices," the paper quoted Espiritu Santo state Governor Vitor Buaiz as saying. "The negotiations are not resolving our problems."
Ministry Executive-Secretary Pedro Parente said some states have already voluntarily signed preliminary debt renegotiation accords, according to Folha.
Parente said he was baffled by the governors' new stance, adding that all new rules for rolling over state debts would be presented to Congress as well as state legislatures anyway, the paper said.
